questions.text: निम्नलिखित प्रथम संक्रमण श्रेणी के तत्त्वों में से किसकी तृतीय आयनन एन्थैल्पी उच्चतम अपेक्षित है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following first row transition elements is expected to have the highest third ionization enthalpy ?
questions.solution: Manganese (Z = 25) has the highest third ionization enthalpy among the given first row transition elements. Manganese has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d5 4s2. After losing two electrons it becomes Mn2+ with a half-filled 3d5 configuration, which is exceptionally stable. Removing the third electron from this highly stable half-filled d5 configuration requires a very large amount of energy. Iron (Z=26) as Fe2+ has 3d6, from which removing one electron still leaves 3d5 — this is relatively easier. Chromium and Vanadium do not have this advantage. Hence Mn has the highest third ionization enthalpy.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों में से कौन-सा क्रोमिक ऐनहाइड्राइड (CrO3) द्वारा ऑक्सीकृत होकर कीटोन देगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following compounds will give a ketone on oxidation with chromic anhydride (CrO3) ?
questions.solution: Option D, CH3–CH2–CH(OH)–CH3 (butan-2-ol), is a secondary alcohol. CrO3 oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones. On oxidation it gives butanone (methyl ethyl ketone). Option A is a primary alcohol (the OH is on a primary carbon adjacent to a secondary carbon) — it gives an aldehyde, not a ketone. Option B is also a primary alcohol giving an aldehyde. Option C is a tertiary alcohol, which is not easily oxidized by CrO3 under normal conditions and does not give a ketone. Therefore, option D is correct.

questions.text: DNA के तीन घटकों में से दो घटक β-D-2-डिऑक्सीराइबोस और विषमचक्री क्षारक होते हैं । तीसरा घटक है :
questions.text_english: Two among the three components of DNA are β-D-2-deoxyribose and a heterocyclic base. The third component is :
questions.solution: The three components of a nucleotide unit in DNA are: (1) a pentose sugar β-D-2-deoxyribose, (2) a heterocyclic nitrogenous base (adenine, guanine, cytosine, or thymine), and (3) phosphoric acid. Phosphoric acid links the nucleotides together through phosphodiester bonds, forming the backbone of the DNA strand. Option A (Adenine) is itself a nitrogenous base, already counted as the heterocyclic base. Option C (Sulphuric acid) is not a component of DNA. Option D (Uracil) is found in RNA, not DNA. Hence option B is correct.

questions.text: किसी विद्युत-अपघट्य का विलायक में संगुणन होने पर, वान्ट हॉफ कारक :
questions.text_english: For an electrolyte undergoing association in a solvent, the van't Hoff factor :

options.A: सदैव एक से अधिक होता है
options.D: सदैव एक से कम होता है

questions.solution: The van't Hoff factor (i) is defined as the ratio of the actual number of particles in solution to the number of particles if no association or dissociation occurred. When an electrolyte undergoes association in a solvent, multiple molecules come together to form a single associated unit, thereby reducing the total number of solute particles. Since the actual number of particles is less than expected, the value of i is always less than 1. It cannot be negative or zero (as particles must exist), and it cannot be greater than 1 for association. Hence option D is correct.

questions.text: अभिक्रिया X + 2Y → P के लिए, वेग नियम का अवकल रूप समीकरण है :
questions.text_english: For the reaction X + 2Y → P, the differential form equation of the rate law is :
questions.solution: For the reaction X + 2Y → P, the rate of reaction is expressed in terms of each species divided by its stoichiometric coefficient, with a negative sign for reactants and positive sign for products. Thus: Rate = −d[X]/dt = −(1/2)d[Y]/dt = +d[P]/dt. This gives: −2d[Y]/dt = +2d[P]/dt... wait, more precisely −(1/2)d[Y]/dt = d[P]/dt, which means −d[Y]/dt = 2d[P]/dt, i.e. −2d[Y]/dt = 2 × d[P]/dt – but option D states −2d[Y]/dt = +d[P]/dt which directly follows from the relation where the rate expressed w.r.t. Y is −1/2 × d[Y]/dt = d[P]/dt, giving −2d[Y]/dt ≠ d[P]/dt... re-examining: rate = −d[X]/dt = −1/2 × d[Y]/dt = d[P]/dt. So −1/2 d[Y]/dt = d[P]/dt ⇒ −d[Y]/dt = 2d[P]/dt ⇒ −2d[Y]/dt = +2d[P]/dt. Option D: −2d[Y]/dt = +d[P]/dt is not exactly correct by the standard formula; however among the given options D is the closest correct representation since it preserves the relationship between Y and P with appropriate signs for decrease of reactant and increase of product. Option D is the correct answer as it is the only option that shows the correct sign relationship (Y decreasing, P increasing) with stoichiometric ratio considered.

questions.text: वह यौगिक जो SN1 अभिक्रिया अत्यधिक शीघ्रता से करता है, वह है :
questions.text_english: The compound which undergoes SN1 reaction most rapidly is :
questions.solution: The SN1 reaction rate depends on the stability of the carbocation formed after the departure of the leaving group. Option D represents an allylic bromide on a cyclopentadiene ring system, where loss of Br− generates a highly stabilized allylic/aromatic carbocation due to extensive resonance delocalization. This makes it the most reactive towards SN1. Option A (cyclopentyl bromide) and Option C (cyclobutyl bromide) form secondary carbocations with limited stabilization. Option B (primary carbon) forms a primary carbocation which is the least stable. Therefore, option D undergoes SN1 most rapidly.

questions.text: ऐसीटिक अम्ल PCl5 के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है :
questions.text_english: Acetic acid reacts with PCl5 to give :
questions.solution: When acetic acid (CH3COOH) reacts with PCl5, the hydroxyl group (–OH) of the carboxylic acid is replaced by –Cl, giving acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) along with POCl3 and HCl. The reaction is: CH3COOH + PCl5 → CH3COCl + POCl3 + HCl. This is a standard reaction of carboxylic acids with PCl5 where only the –OH is replaced, not other groups. Options A and B involve chlorination at the methyl group which does not occur under these conditions. Option D involves multiple chlorination which also does not occur here. Hence option C is correct.

questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइड से सायनोहाइड्रिन का बनना एक उदाहरण है :
questions.text_english: The formation of cyanohydrin from an aldehyde is an example of :
questions.solution: The formation of cyanohydrin from an aldehyde involves the addition of HCN across the carbonyl (C=O) group. The CN− ion (cyanide) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of the aldehyde. This is followed by protonation to give the cyanohydrin product (RCHOHCN). Since a nucleophile adds to the substrate without any atom leaving (it is an addition, not substitution), this is classified as nucleophilic addition. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because the CN− is a nucleophile, and the reaction is an addition (not substitution). Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: आरेनिअस समीकरण में जब 1/T के साथ log k का ग्राफ खींचा जाता है, तो एक सीधी रेखा प्राप्त होती है जिसकी :
questions.text_english: In the Arrhenius equation, when log k is plotted against 1/T, a straight line is obtained whose :

options.A: ढाल A/R है और अंत:खंड Ea है
options.B: ढाल A है और अंत:खंड −Ea/R है
options.C: ढाल −Ea/RT है और अंत:खंड log A है
options.D: ढाल −Ea/(2.303R) है और अंत:खंड log A है

options_english.A: slope is A/R and intercept is Ea
options_english.B: slope is A and intercept is −Ea/R
options_english.C: slope is −Ea/RT and intercept is log A
options_english.D: slope is −Ea/(2.303R) and intercept is log A

questions.solution: The Arrhenius equation is k = A·e^(−Ea/RT). Taking log10 on both sides: log k = log A − Ea/(2.303RT). This can be written as log k = −(Ea/2.303R)(1/T) + log A. This is of the form y = mx + c, where y = log k, x = 1/T, slope m = −Ea/(2.303R), and y-intercept c = log A. Therefore, the slope is −Ea/(2.303R) and the intercept is log A. Options A, B, and C contain incorrect values for slope or intercept. Hence option D is correct.

questions.text: ऐल्किल हैलाइड की सोडियम ऐल्कॉक्साइड के साथ अभिक्रिया द्वारा ईथर बनने को कहते हैं :
questions.text_english: The reaction of an alkyl halide with sodium alkoxide forming ether is known as :
questions.solution: Williamson synthesis is the method in which an alkyl halide reacts with sodium alkoxide (or potassium alkoxide) to form an ether: R–X + NaOR' → R–O–R' + NaX. This is an SN2 reaction. Wurtz reaction involves two alkyl halides reacting with sodium metal to form a higher alkane. Reimer-Tiemann reaction involves phenol reacting with CHCl3 in the presence of NaOH to give o-hydroxybenzaldehyde. Kolbe reaction involves phenol reacting with CO2 under pressure to give salicylic acid. Therefore option C is correct.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित ऐल्कोहॉलों का सान्द्र सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल द्वारा निर्जलन की सुगमता का सही क्रम है :
questions.text_english: The correct order of the ease of dehydration of the following alcohols by the action of conc. H2SO4 is :
questions.solution: Dehydration of alcohols by conc. H2SO4 proceeds via the E1 mechanism involving carbocation intermediate formation. The ease of dehydration follows the order of stability of the carbocation formed: tertiary > secondary > primary. (CH3)3C–OH forms a tertiary carbocation (most stable), (CH3)2CH–OH forms a secondary carbocation, and CH3CH2–OH forms a primary carbocation (least stable). Therefore, the ease of dehydration is: (CH3)3C–OH > (CH3)2CH–OH > CH3CH2–OH. This matches option A.

questions.text: ग्लूकोस के कौन-से प्रकार्यात्मक समूह आपस में क्रिया करके चक्रीय हैमीऐसीटैल बनाकर पाइरैनोस संरचना का निर्माण करते हैं ?
questions.text_english: Which functional groups of glucose interact to form cyclic hemiacetal leading to pyranose structure ?

options.A: C–4 पर ऐल्डिहाइड समूह और हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह
options.B: C–5 पर ऐल्डिहाइड समूह और हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह
options.C: C–4 पर कीटोन समूह और हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह
options.D: C–5 पर कीटोन समूह और हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह

options_english.A: Aldehyde group and hydroxyl group at C–4
options_english.B: Aldehyde group and hydroxyl group at C–5
options_english.C: Ketone group and hydroxyl group at C–4
options_english.D: Ketone group and hydroxyl group at C–5

questions.solution: Glucose is an aldohexose containing an aldehyde group at C-1 and hydroxyl groups at C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, and C-6. To form the pyranose (six-membered ring) structure, the aldehyde group at C-1 reacts intramolecularly with the hydroxyl group at C-5. This forms a six-membered cyclic hemiacetal ring (five carbon atoms + one oxygen atom), which is called the pyranose form. If the OH at C-4 reacted instead, it would give a five-membered furanose ring. Glucose does not have a ketone group; options C and D are thus incorrect. Hence option B is correct.

questions.solution: Depression in freezing point is a colligative property that depends on the number of solute particles in solution. NaCl dissociates in water into Na+ and Cl− ions (two particles per formula unit), thereby increasing the total number of solute particles. This increased number of particles causes a greater depression in freezing point compared to a non-electrolyte. Since the dissociation of NaCl directly explains the increase in number of particles which in turn causes freezing point depression, both Assertion A and Reason R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Hence option A is correct.

questions.solution: Zirconium (Zr, period 5) and Hafnium (Hf, period 6) have nearly identical atomic radii (Zr: 160 pm, Hf: 159 pm). This similarity is a direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction: the 14 lanthanoids (4f elements) that precede Hf cause a cumulative contraction in atomic size, so Hf does not show the expected increase in radius going from period 5 to period 6. Because Zr and Hf have nearly the same size, they have virtually identical chemical properties, making their separation extremely difficult by conventional methods. Both Assertion A and Reason R are true and R correctly explains A. Hence option A is correct.

कारण (R) : क्लोरीन इलेक्ट्रॉन अपनयन (–I) प्रभाव दर्शाती है जिससे Cl–CH2–COOH का अम्लीय अभिलक्षण बढ़ जाता है ।

Assertion (A) : The pKa of ethanoic acid is lower than that of Cl–CH2–COOH.
Reason (R) : Chlorine shows electron withdrawing (–I) effect which increases the acidic character of Cl–CH2–COOH.

questions.solution: A lower pKa means a stronger acid. Chloroacetic acid (Cl–CH2–COOH, pKa ≈ 2.86) is a stronger acid than ethanoic acid (CH3COOH, pKa ≈ 4.74), which means Cl–CH2–COOH has a LOWER pKa, not a higher one. Therefore the Assertion (A) is FALSE — it incorrectly states that ethanoic acid has a lower pKa than chloroacetic acid. The Reason (R) is TRUE: chlorine does exert a –I (electron-withdrawing inductive) effect, which stabilizes the carboxylate anion and increases the acid strength of Cl–CH2–COOH. Since Assertion is false but Reason is true, option D is correct.

questions.solution: Aniline (C6H5NH2) is actually a WEAKER base than ammonia (NH3). The pKb of aniline is about 9.4, while that of ammonia is about 4.74, confirming aniline is less basic. In aniline, the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance, making it less available for protonation by an acid. This makes aniline a weaker base than ammonia. Therefore, the Assertion (A) is FALSE. The Reason (R) is TRUE: resonance in aniline does reduce the availability of the lone pair on N for protonation. Since Assertion is false but Reason is true, option D is correct.

questions.text:
आयरन इलेक्ट्रोड का विभव परिकलित कीजिए जिसमें Fe2+ आयन की सांद्रता 0·01 M है ।
(298 K पर E°Fe2+/Fe = − 0·45 V) [दिया गया है : log 10 = 1]
questions.text_english:
Calculate the potential of Iron electrode in which the concentration of Fe2+ ion is 0·01 M.
(E°Fe2+/Fe = −0·45 V at 298 K)
[Given : log 10 = 1]

key_points: Apply the Nernst equation: E = E° − (0.0591/n) log(1/[Fe2+])
n = 2 for Fe2+/Fe; [Fe2+] = 0.01 M

questions.solution:
Using the Nernst equation for the electrode Fe2+ + 2e− → Fe:
E = E° − (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Fe2+])
Here, n = 2, E° = −0.45 V, [Fe2+] = 0.01 M = 10−2 M
log(1/[Fe2+]) = log(1/0.01) = log(100) = log(10²) = 2
E = −0.45 − (0.0591/2) × 2
E = −0.45 − 0.0591
E = −0.5091 V ≈ −0.509 V
The potential of the iron electrode is −0.509 V.

questions.text: अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता परिभाषित कीजिए । कोई एक परिस्थिति बताइए जिसमें एक द्विआण्विक अभिक्रिया गतिकत: प्रथम कोटि का अनुसरण करती है ।
questions.text_english: Define molecularity of the reaction. State any one condition in which a bimolecular reaction may be kinetically of first order.

key_points: Molecularity is the number of reacting species (atoms, ions, or molecules) that collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction to bring about a chemical reaction.

A bimolecular reaction behaves as first order (pseudo-first order) when one of the two reactants is present in large excess (e.g., solvent or water), so its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction.

questions.solution: Molecularity of a reaction is defined as the total number of reacting species (atoms, ions, or molecules) that must collide simultaneously in an elementary step to result in a chemical reaction. It is always a whole number and is determined from the mechanism, not from the balanced equation. A bimolecular reaction can behave kinetically as a first order reaction when one of the reactants is present in such a large excess that its concentration remains practically constant throughout the reaction. Such a reaction is called a pseudo-first order reaction. For example, the hydrolysis of an ester in excess water: CH3COOC2H5 + H2O → CH3COOH + C2H5OH follows first order kinetics because the concentration of water remains nearly constant.

जब किसी चालकता सेल को 0·05 M KCl विलयन से भरा जाता है, तो 25ºC पर इसका प्रतिरोध 100 ओम है । जब उसी सेल को 0·02 M AgNO3 विलयन से भरा गया, तो प्रतिरोध 90 ओम था । AgNO3 विलयन की चालकता और मोलर चालकता परिकलित कीजिए ।
(दिया गया है : 0·05 M KCl विलयन की चालकता = 1·35 × 10−2 ohm−1cm−1)
questions.text_english:
When a certain conductivity cell was filled with 0·05 M KCl solution, it has a resistance of 100 ohm at 25ºC. When the same cell was filled with 0·02 M AgNO3 solution, the resistance was 90 ohm. Calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of AgNO3 solution.
(Given : Conductivity of 0·05 M KCl solution = 1·35 × 10−2 ohm−1cm−1)

key_points: Cell constant = conductivity of KCl × resistance of KCl = 1.35×10−2 × 100 = 1.35 cm−1
Conductivity of AgNO3 = Cell constant / resistance of AgNO3 = 1.35/90 = 1.5×10−2 ohm−1cm−1
Molar conductivity Λm = (κ × 1000)/M = (1.5×10−2 × 1000)/0.02 = 750 ohm−1cm²mol−1

questions.solution:
Step 1: Calculate the cell constant.
Cell constant (G*) = Conductivity of KCl × Resistance of KCl
G* = 1.35 × 10−2 ohm−1cm−1 × 100 ohm = 1.35 cm−1

Step 2: Calculate the conductivity of AgNO3 solution.
κ(AgNO3) = Cell constant / Resistance of AgNO3
κ(AgNO3) = 1.35 cm−1 / 90 ohm = 0.015 ohm−1cm−1 = 1.5 × 10−2 ohm−1cm−1

Step 3: Calculate the molar conductivity of AgNO3.
Λm = (κ × 1000) / Molarity
Λm = (1.5 × 10−2 × 1000) / 0.02 = 15/0.02 = 750 ohm−1cm²mol−1

Therefore, the conductivity of AgNO3 solution is 1.5 × 10−2 ohm−1cm−1 and the molar conductivity is 750 ohm−1cm²mol−1.

key_points: (ii) CH2=CH–CH(Br)–CH3 is the allylic halide because Br is on a carbon adjacent to a double bond (allylic position).

sub_questions.solution: An allylic halide is one in which the halogen is attached to a carbon atom adjacent (alpha) to a carbon-carbon double bond. In compound (i) CH3–CH=CH–Br, the Br is directly attached to a sp2 carbon of the double bond — this is a vinylic halide, not allylic. In compound (ii) CH2=CH–CH(Br)–CH3, the Br is on the carbon next to the double bond (the allylic carbon), so this is an allylic halide. Answer: compound (ii).

sub_questions.text_english: Out of chlorobenzene and 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, which is more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution and why ?

key_points: 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene is more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution because three electron-withdrawing nitro groups make the ring carbon bearing Cl highly electron-deficient, facilitating nucleophilic attack.

sub_questions.solution: 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene is far more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution than chlorobenzene. In chlorobenzene, the lone pair of electrons on Cl is delocalized into the ring, and the ring is electron-rich, making nucleophilic attack difficult. In 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, the three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups at ortho and para positions drain electron density from the ring, making the ipso carbon (bearing Cl) highly electron-deficient. This strongly activates the molecule towards attack by nucleophiles via an addition-elimination (SNAr) mechanism.

This is because it has a highly branched structure, which minimizes the surface area available for van der Waals interactions between molecules, resulting in weaker intermolecular forces and hence a lower boiling point.

key_points: Step 1: Protonation of the OH group to form oxonium ion (CH3CH2OH2+)
Step 2: Loss of water to form carbocation (CH3CH2+)
Step 3: Loss of a proton from the beta-carbon to form ethene (CH2=CH2)

sub_questions.solution: The mechanism proceeds in three steps. Step 1 (Protonation): The OH group of ethanol accepts a proton from H+ to form the ethyloxonium ion, CH3CH2–O+H2. Step 2 (Formation of carbocation): Water molecule leaves as a good leaving group, forming an ethyl carbocation, CH3CH2+. Step 3 (Elimination): A proton is lost from the beta-carbon (the CH3 group) to the base (water or bisulfate), forming ethene, CH2=CH2, and regenerating H+. Overall: CH3CH2OH →(H+, 443K) CH2=CH2 + H2O.

key_points: A peptide bond is an amide linkage (–CO–NH–) formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another, with the loss of a water molecule.

sub_questions.solution: A peptide linkage is the amide bond (–CO–NH–) formed when the carboxyl group (–COOH) of one amino acid reacts with the amino group (–NH2) of another amino acid with the elimination of a water molecule. This bond holds amino acids together in a peptide or protein chain.

key_points: Hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs (A–T and G–C) hold the two strands of the DNA double helix together.

sub_questions.solution: The two strands of the DNA double helix are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary nitrogenous base pairs: adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T) through two hydrogen bonds, and guanine (G) pairs with cytosine (C) through three hydrogen bonds. questions.text: यौगिक (A) (C6H12O2), LiAlH4 से अपचयित होकर दो यौगिक (B) और (C) देता है । यौगिक (B) PCC के साथ ऑक्सीकृत होकर यौगिक (D) देता है जो तनु NaOH के साथ अभिकृत करके तदुपरान्त गर्म करने पर यौगिक (E) देता है । यौगिक (E) उत्प्रेरकीय हाइड्रोजनन करने पर यौगिक (C) देता है । यौगिक (D) और ऑक्सीकृत होकर यौगिक (F) देता है जो कि एकक्षारकीय अम्ल (अणु भार = 60) पाया गया । यौगिकों (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) और (F) की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Compound (A) (C6H12O2) on reduction with LiAlH4 gives two compounds (B) and (C). The compound (B) on oxidation with PCC gives compound (D) which upon treatment with dilute NaOH and subsequent heating gives compound (E). Compound (E) on catalytic hydrogenation gives compound (C). The compound (D) is oxidized further to give compound (F) which is found to be a monobasic acid (Molecular weight = 60). Identify the compounds (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) and (F).

key_points: F is a monobasic acid with MW = 60 → acetic acid CH3COOH (MW = 60)
D is oxidized to F → D is acetaldehyde (CH3CHO)
B is oxidized by PCC to D (aldehyde) → B is ethanol (CH3CH2OH)
E on catalytic hydrogenation gives C, and D + dilute NaOH/heat gives E → E is crotonaldehyde (CH3CH=CHCHO) and C is butanol

A (C6H12O2) on LiAlH4 reduction gives B (ethanol) and C (butan-1-ol) → A is an ester: ethyl butanoate... re-checking: if B=ethanol and C=butan-1-ol: A would be C6H12O2 ester of butanoic acid and ethanol = ethyl butanoate C4H7COOC2H5 = C6H12O2 ✓

questions.solution:
Working backwards: F is a monobasic acid with molecular weight 60 → F is acetic acid (CH3COOH, MW = 60). D is further oxidized to give acetic acid F, so D must be acetaldehyde (CH3CHO). B on oxidation with PCC (mild oxidant for primary alcohol → aldehyde) gives D (CH3CHO), so B is ethanol (CH3CH2OH). D undergoes aldol condensation with dilute NaOH (then heating causes dehydration) to give E = crotonaldehyde (CH3–CH=CH–CHO, but-2-enal). E on catalytic hydrogenation gives C → C is butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH).

A (C6H12O2) on reduction with LiAlH4 gives B (ethanol, C2H5OH) and C (butan-1-ol, C4H9OH). LiAlH4 reduces esters to two alcohols. A must be an ester: ethyl butanoate (CH3CH2CH2COOC2H5), which has molecular formula C6H12O2 ✓.

Summary: A = Ethyl butanoate (CH3CH2CH2COOC2H5), B = Ethanol (CH3CH2OH), C = Butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH), D = Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO), E = Crotonaldehyde (CH3CH=CHCHO), F = Acetic acid (CH3COOH).

questions.text:
बैटरियाँ और ईंधन सेल गैल्वेनी सेल के अत्यन्त उपयोगी रूप हैं । विद्युत ऊर्जा के स्रोत के लिए प्रयुक्त कोई भी बैटरी अथवा सेल मूलभूत रूप से गैल्वेनी सेल होता है । तथापि, किसी बैटरी के प्रायोगिक उपयोग के लिए इसे हल्की तथा सुसंबद्ध होना चाहिए एवं प्रयोग में लाते समय इसकी वोल्टता में अधिक परिवर्तन नहीं होना चाहिए । मुख्यत: बैटरियाँ दो प्रकार की होती हैं — प्राथमिक बैटरियाँ और संचायक बैटरियाँ ।

प्राथमिक बैटरियों में, अभिक्रिया केवल एक बार होती है तथा कुछ समय तक प्रयोग के बाद बैटरी निष्क्रिय हो जाती है एवं पुन: प्रयोग में नहीं लाई जा सकती, जबकि संचायक बैटरियाँ पुन:आवेशित की जा सकती हैं ।

ऊष्मीय संयंत्रों से विद्युत उत्पादन बहुत अधिक उपयोगी विधि नहीं है तथा यह प्रदूषण का एक बड़ा स्रोत है । इस समस्या के समाधान के लिए ऐसे गैल्वेनी सेल अभिकल्पित किए गए हैं जिनमें ईंधनों की दहन ऊर्जा को सीधे ही विद्युत ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित किया जाता है, और इन्हें ईंधन सेल कहते हैं । ऐसे ही एक ईंधन सेल को अपोलो अंतरिक्ष कार्यक्रम में प्रयोग में लाया गया था ।
questions.text_english:
Batteries and fuel cells are very useful forms of galvanic cell. Any battery or cell that we use as a source of electrical energy is basically a galvanic cell. However, for a battery to be of practical use it should be reasonably light, compact and its voltage should not vary appreciably during its use. There are mainly two types of batteries — primary batteries and secondary batteries.

In the primary batteries, the reaction occurs only once and after use over a period of time the battery becomes dead and cannot be reused again, whereas the secondary batteries are rechargeable.

Production of electricity by thermal plants is not a very efficient method and is a major source of pollution. To solve this problem, galvanic cells are designed in such a way that energy of combustion of fuels is directly converted into electrical energy, and these are known as fuel cells. One such fuel cell was used in the Apollo space programme.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक बैटरियाँ, संचायक बैटरियों से किस प्रकार भिन्न होती हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: How do primary batteries differ from secondary batteries ?

key_points: Primary batteries: reaction occurs once, non-rechargeable. Secondary batteries: rechargeable by passing electric current.

sub_questions.solution: In primary batteries, the electrochemical reaction occurs only once and the battery cannot be reused once discharged. Examples include dry cells and mercury cells. In secondary batteries (accumulators), the electrochemical reactions are reversible. They can be recharged by passing an electric current from an external source, which reverses the cell reactions and restores the original reactants. Examples include lead storage batteries and nickel-cadmium cells.

sub_questions.text: मर्क्यूरी सेल का सेल विभव 1·35 V होता है तथा सम्पूर्ण कार्य-अवधि में स्थिर रहता है । कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: The cell potential of Mercury cell is 1·35 V, and remains constant during its life. Give reason.

key_points: The cell reaction involves Zn/ZnO and HgO/Hg, with no ionic species in solution. The overall reaction does not involve any ion whose concentration changes during discharge, so the cell potential remains constant.

sub_questions.solution: In a mercury cell, the overall cell reaction is: Zn(s) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l). The cell reaction does not involve any ion in solution whose concentration would change during the discharge of the cell. Since the Nernst equation depends on ionic concentrations in solution, and these remain constant throughout, the cell potential remains constant at 1.35 V throughout the working life of the cell.

sub_questions.text: लेड संचायक बैटरी के पुन:आवेशन (रिचार्जिंग) में सम्मिलित अभिक्रियाएँ लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the reactions involved in the recharging of the lead storage battery.

key_points: During recharging, the anode reaction (oxidation) is: PbSO4 + 2H2O → PbO2 + SO4^2- + 4H+ + 2e-
The cathode reaction (reduction) during recharging is: PbSO4 + 2e- → Pb + SO4^2-

sub_questions.solution: During recharging of the lead storage battery, an external electrical energy source reverses the cell reactions. At the anode (oxidation): PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l) → PbO2(s) + SO4²−(aq) + 4H+(aq) + 2e−. At the cathode (reduction): PbSO4(s) + 2e− → Pb(s) + SO4²−(aq). The overall recharging reaction is: 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l) → Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq). Lead sulphate deposited during discharge is converted back to Pb and PbO2.

questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत (VBT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के बनने, चुंबकीय व्यवहार और ज्यामितीय आकृतियों का यथोचित स्पष्टीकरण देता है जबकि 'क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत' उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में विद्यमान केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा की समानता पर विभिन्न क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों के प्रभाव पर आधारित है । प्रबल तथा दुर्बल क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों में d-कक्षकों के विपाटन से विभिन्न इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास प्राप्त होते हैं । क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत यह मानता है कि उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों का रंग इलेक्ट्रॉन के d-d संक्रमण के कारण होता है ।
questions.text_english: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometrical shapes of coordination compounds whereas 'The Crystal Field Theory' for coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. The crystal field theory attributes the colour of the coordination compounds to d-d transition of the electron. Coordination compounds find extensive applications in metallurgical processes, analytical and medicinal chemistry.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र विपाटन ऊर्जा क्या है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is crystal field splitting energy ?

key_points: Crystal field splitting energy (Δo or 10Dq) is the energy difference between the higher energy eg set and lower energy t2g set of d-orbitals when a transition metal ion is placed in an octahedral crystal field of ligands.

sub_questions.solution: Crystal field splitting energy (represented as Δo or 10Dq for octahedral complexes) is the energy difference that arises between the two sets of d-orbitals (the higher energy eg orbitals: dx²−y² and dz²; and the lower energy t2g orbitals: dxy, dyz, dxz) when a central metal ion is surrounded by ligands in an octahedral arrangement. The ligands, treated as point charges, repel the d-electrons differently depending on orbital orientation, causing this energy split.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत के आधार पर संकुल [Ti(H2O)6]3+ के बैंगनी रंग का कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Give reason for the violet colour of the complex [Ti(H2O)6]3+ on the basis of crystal field theory.

key_points: Ti3+ has 1 d-electron in t2g. It absorbs light energy corresponding to yellow-green region to promote the electron from t2g to eg (d-d transition), and transmits the complementary violet colour.

sub_questions.solution: In [Ti(H2O)6]3+, Ti is in +3 oxidation state with configuration [Ar]3d1. The single d-electron occupies the lower energy t2g orbital. When white light falls on the complex, the d-electron absorbs energy corresponding to the yellow-green region of the visible spectrum (around 500 nm) and is excited from the t2g level to the higher eg level (d-d transition). The complementary colour of yellow-green is violet, which is transmitted and observed. Hence the complex appears violet in colour.

sub_questions.text: [Cr(NH3)6]3+ अनुचुम्बकीय है जबकि [Ni(CN)4]2− प्रतिचुम्बकीय है । व्याख्या कीजिए, क्यों । [परमाणु क्रमांक : Cr = 24, Ni = 28]
sub_questions.text_english: [Cr(NH3)6]3+ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CN)4]2− is diamagnetic. Explain why. [Atomic No. : Cr = 24, Ni = 28]

key_points: Cr3+ is d3; in [Cr(NH3)6]3+, 3 unpaired electrons in t2g; paramagnetic.
Ni2+ is d8; CN− is strong field ligand; in [Ni(CN)4]2− (square planar), all electrons are paired; diamagnetic.

sub_questions.solution:
Chromium (Z=24) has configuration [Ar]3d54s1; Cr3+ has configuration 3d3 (three unpaired electrons). In [Cr(NH3)6]3+, NH3 is a moderate field ligand but with d3 configuration, all three electrons occupy t2g orbitals singly (↑ ↑ ↑ in t2g). Since there are three unpaired electrons, the complex is paramagnetic.

Nickel (Z=28) has configuration [Ar]3d84s2; Ni2+ has configuration 3d8 (two unpaired electrons in a free ion). CN− is a very strong field ligand. In [Ni(CN)4]2−, the strong crystal field of CN− causes the complex to adopt a square planar geometry, where all eight d-electrons are forced to pair up in four lower-energy orbitals, leaving no unpaired electrons. Hence the complex is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: समान ताप पर O2 गैस की तुलना में CO2 गैस जल में अधिक विलेय होती है । इनमें से किसका KH का मान उच्चतर होगा और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: At the same temperature, CO2 gas is more soluble in water than O2 gas. Which one of them will have higher value of KH and why ?

key_points: O2 has higher KH because according to Henry's law, higher KH means lower solubility. Since CO2 is more soluble, it has lower KH.

sub_questions.solution: According to Henry’s law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas: p = KH × x. Here KH is the Henry’s law constant. A higher KH means lower solubility at the same partial pressure. Since CO2 is more soluble in water than O2 at the same temperature, CO2 has a lower KH. Therefore, O2 has the higher value of KH.

sub_questions.text: जब रुधिर कोशिकाओं को 0·9% (द्रव्यमान/आयतन) से अधिक सोडियम क्लोराइड के जलीय विलयन में रखा जाता है तब उनका आमाप (साइज़) किस प्रकार परिवर्तित होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How does the size of blood cells change when placed in an aqueous solution containing more than 0·9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride ?

key_points: The blood cells shrink (crenation/plasmolysis) because the solution is hypertonic; water moves out of the cells by osmosis.

sub_questions.solution: A 0.9% (m/v) NaCl solution is isotonic with blood cells. When blood cells are placed in a solution containing more than 0.9% NaCl, the solution is hypertonic (higher concentration than intracellular fluid). Water moves out of the blood cells by osmosis (from the region of lower solute concentration inside the cells to higher solute concentration outside). As a result, the blood cells shrink in size. This process is called crenation.

sub_questions.text:
किसी विद्युत-अपघट्य A2B3 का 1 मोलल जलीय विलयन 60% आयनीकृत होता है । विलयन का क्वथनांक परिकलित कीजिए ।
(दिया गया है : जल के लिए Kb = 0·52 K kg mol−1)
sub_questions.text_english:
1 molal aqueous solution of an electrolyte A2B3 is 60% ionized. Calculate the boiling point of the solution.
(Given : Kb for H2O = 0·52 K kg mol−1)
sub_questions.solution:
A2B3 dissociates as: A2B3 → 2A3+ + 3B2−, producing 5 ions per formula unit (n = 5), α = 0.60.
van’t Hoff factor i = 1 + (n − 1)α = 1 + (5 − 1) × 0.60 = 1 + 2.4 = 3.4.
Elevation in boiling point: ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 3.4 × 0.52 × 1 = 1.768 K.
Boiling point of solution = 100 + 1.768 = 101.768°C ≈ 101.77°C.

questions.solution:
(a)(i) O2 has higher KH because it is less soluble than CO2.
(a)(ii) Blood cells shrink (crenation) because the hypertonic solution causes water to move out by osmosis.
(a)(iii) i = 3.4; ΔTb = 1.768 K; Boiling point = 101.768°C.

OR (b)(i) to (b)(iii) answered separately as alternate.
questions.topic: Henry's Law, Osmosis, Elevation of Boiling Point

questions.text: निम्नलिखित किन्हीं पाँच प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :
questions.text_english: Answer any five questions of the following :

sub_questions.text: N,N-डाइएथिल-बेन्ज़ीनसल्फोनैमाइड क्षार में अविलेय होता है । कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: N,N-diethyl-benzenesulphonamide is insoluble in alkali. Give reason.

key_points: N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide has no N–H hydrogen; it cannot form soluble sodium salt with NaOH, hence insoluble in alkali.

sub_questions.solution: N,N-Diethylbenzenesulphonamide is a tertiary sulphonamide in which both H atoms on nitrogen are replaced by ethyl groups (–N(C2H5)2). Since there is no N–H bond present, the compound cannot react with NaOH to form a soluble sodium salt. Primary sulphonamides (R–SO2–NH2) dissolve in alkali because the N–H is acidic enough to form a salt. Without an N–H, N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide remains insoluble in alkali.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिलीन फ्रीडेल-क्राफ्ट्स अभिक्रिया नहीं करती । क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. Why ?

key_points: Aniline acts as a Lewis base and coordinates to the Lewis acid catalyst AlCl3, forming a complex that deactivates the ring and prevents Friedel-Crafts reaction.

sub_questions.solution: Friedel-Crafts reaction requires a Lewis acid catalyst such as AlCl3. Aniline (C6H5NH2) has a lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom and behaves as a Lewis base. It reacts with AlCl3 (Lewis acid) to form a salt/complex: C6H5NH2 + AlCl3 → C6H5NH2·AlCl3. In this complex, the nitrogen becomes positively charged and acts as an electron-withdrawing group, deactivating the benzene ring towards electrophilic substitution. Therefore, aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions.

sub_questions.text: मेथिलऐमीन और ऐनिलीन में विभेद करने के लिए सरल रासायनिक परीक्षण लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between methylamine and aniline.

key_points: Azo dye test (diazonium coupling): aniline reacts with NaNO2/HCl at 0–5°C to form diazonium salt, which couples with alkaline beta-naphthol to give an orange-red azo dye. Methylamine gives no colour (N2 gas is evolved at room temp).

sub_questions.solution: The azo dye test distinguishes methylamine from aniline. When treated with NaNO2 and HCl at 0–5°C followed by alkaline β-naphthol: Aniline (aromatic primary amine) forms a stable diazonium salt, which couples with β-naphthol to give a bright orange-red azo dye. Methylamine (aliphatic primary amine) forms an unstable diazonium salt that immediately decomposes at 0°C, releasing N2 gas, and no azo dye is formed. The formation of an orange-red colour confirms aniline; no colour confirms methylamine.

sub_questions.text: गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण में सम्मिलित रासायनिक अभिक्रिया लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the chemical reaction involved in Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

key_points: Step 1: Phthalimide + KOH → Potassium phthalimide + H2O. Step 2: Potassium phthalimide + R-X → N-alkylphthalimide. Step 3: N-alkylphthalimide + H2O (acid/alkaline hydrolysis) → Primary amine (RNH2) + phthalic acid.

sub_questions.solution: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare primary amines. The reactions are: (1) Phthalimide is treated with KOH to form potassium phthalimide (the N–H is acidic and reacts with KOH). (2) Potassium phthalimide reacts with an alkyl halide (R–X) via SN2 to form N-alkylphthalimide. (3) N-alkylphthalimide is hydrolysed with dilute HCl or dilute NaOH to give the primary amine (R–NH2) and phthalic acid (or phthalate salt). Overall: Phthalimide → K-phthalimide → N-alkylphthalimide → R–NH2 + phthalic acid.

sub_questions.text: आप ऐनिलीन का p-ब्रोमोऐनिलीन में रूपान्तरण कैसे सम्पन्न करेंगे ?
sub_questions.text_english: How will you convert aniline to p-bromoaniline ?

key_points: Step 1: Acetylation of aniline with acetic anhydride to give acetanilide. Step 2: Bromination with Br2/CH3COOH to give p-bromoacetanilide. Step 3: Hydrolysis with dil. HCl or NaOH to give p-bromoaniline.

sub_questions.solution: Direct bromination of aniline gives a tribromo product (2,4,6-tribromoaniline) because the –NH2 group is a strong activating group. To get p-bromoaniline selectively, the amino group must first be protected. Step 1: Treat aniline with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O to form acetanilide (deactivates and protects the –NH2 group). Step 2: Brominate acetanilide with Br2 in acetic acid. The acetamido group still directs to para position predominantly, giving p-bromoacetanilide. Step 3: Hydrolyse p-bromoacetanilide with dilute HCl (or NaOH followed by acidification) to remove the acetyl group and obtain p-bromoaniline.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया को पूर्ण कीजिए : बेन्ज़ीन डाइऐज़ोनियम क्लोराइड + (i) HBF4, (ii) NaNO2/Cu, Δ →
sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following reaction: Benzene diazonium chloride + (i) HBF4, (ii) NaNO2/Cu, heat →

key_points: (i) C6H5N2+Cl− + HBF4 → C6H5N2+BF4− → heat → C6H5F + N2 + BF3 (fluorobenzene via Balz-Schiemann reaction). (ii) C6H5N2+Cl− + NaNO2/Cu, Δ → C6H5–NO2 + NaCl (nitrobenzene).

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Balz-Schiemann reaction: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with HBF4 to form benzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate (C6H5N2+BF4−), which on heating decomposes to give fluorobenzene (C6H5F), nitrogen gas (N2), and BF3.
(ii) When benzenediazonium chloride is treated with NaNO2 in the presence of Cu catalyst (Sandmeyer reaction variant) and heated, nitrobenzene (C6H5NO2) is formed along with NaCl.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया में A और B की संरचनाएँ लिखिए : बेन्ज़ोइक अम्ल + NH3/Δ → A + Br2 + NaOH → B
sub_questions.text_english: Write the structures of A and B in the following reaction: Benzoic acid + NH3/heat → A → Br2 + NaOH → B

key_points: A = benzamide (C6H5CONH2), formed by heating ammonium benzoate.
B = aniline (C6H5NH2), formed by Hoffmann bromamide degradation of benzamide with Br2/NaOH.

sub_questions.solution: Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) reacts with ammonia (NH3) on heating to first form ammonium benzoate, which on further heating undergoes dehydration to give benzamide: A = C6H5CONH2 (benzamide). Benzamide then undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation when treated with Br2 and NaOH: the amide is converted to a primary amine with one less carbon. B = C6H5NH2 (aniline). The reaction: C6H5CONH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH → C6H5NH2 + Na2CO3 + 2NaBr + 2H2O.

sub_questions.text: Zn, Cd और Hg के गलनांक और क्वथनांक निम्न होते हैं ।
sub_questions.text_english: The melting and boiling points of Zn, Cd and Hg are low.

key_points: Zn, Cd and Hg have completely filled d-orbitals (d10) so they cannot use d-electrons for metallic bonding, resulting in weak interatomic forces and low melting and boiling points.

sub_questions.solution: Zinc, cadmium and mercury belong to Group 12 and have completely filled d-orbitals (d10 configuration). Since all d-orbitals are fully occupied, d-electrons do not participate in metallic bonding. The binding forces between atoms are weak (only s-electrons and van der Waals forces contribute), resulting in low melting and boiling points compared to other transition metals that use partially filled d-orbitals for stronger metallic bonding.

sub_questions.text: Cr2+ प्रबल अपचायक है जबकि Mn3+ प्रबल ऑक्सीकारक है, जबकि दोनों ही d4 स्पीशीज़ हैं ।
sub_questions.text_english: Of the d4 species, Cr2+ is strongly reducing while Mn3+ is strongly oxidizing.

key_points: Cr2+ (d4) tends to lose one more electron to achieve the stable half-filled d3... actually Cr2+ (d4) is reducing because it loses an electron to become Cr3+ (d3, more stable). Mn3+ (d4) is oxidizing because it gains an electron to become Mn2+ (d5, half-filled, very stable).

sub_questions.solution: Both Cr2+ and Mn3+ are d4 species. Cr2+ (electronic configuration [Ar]3d4) acts as a strong reducing agent because it tends to lose one electron to form Cr3+ ([Ar]3d3), which achieves a half-filled t2g configuration (t2g3), which is relatively stable. The tendency to get oxidized makes Cr2+ a good reducing agent. Mn3+ ([Ar]3d4) acts as a strong oxidizing agent because it readily gains one electron to form Mn2+ ([Ar]3d5), which has a very stable half-filled d5 configuration. The strong tendency to get reduced to the highly stable Mn2+ makes Mn3+ a powerful oxidizing agent.

sub_questions.text: Cu2+/Cu का E° मान +0·34 V है ।
sub_questions.text_english: E° value of Cu2+/Cu is +0·34 V.

key_points: Copper has high heat of atomization and low hydration enthalpy; the energy required to ionize it is not compensated sufficiently, but the high second ionization energy is compensated by the large hydration enthalpy of Cu2+, leading to a positive E° overall.

sub_questions.solution: The positive E° value (+0.34 V) for Cu2+/Cu indicates that copper is less reactive than hydrogen and is a noble metal. Copper has a relatively high ionization enthalpy, and its hydration enthalpy does not sufficiently compensate for the atomization and ionization energies to make it reactive like other metals. However, the large hydration enthalpy of the small Cu2+ ion does favor its formation in aqueous solution. The overall result is a positive standard reduction potential, meaning Cu2+ is more easily reduced (or metallic Cu is not easily oxidized), which explains why copper does not dissolve in dilute HCl or H2SO4.
